_doc: The full sweep of FULL_SWEEP.txt: every policy on google (top 24 simpoints, 50M warmup + 200M measured), datacenter (memtrace, 10M + 10M) and SPEC 2006/2017/2026 (50M + 10M), the last four at 90% simpoint weight coverage. `fullsweep.py gen STUDY/VARIANT` reads the REPL_MLP gammas from that gsearch result; the architecture and the REPL_MLP base params come from the study's templates. Turn a setup off with "enabled": false or on the command line (--only / --skip).
_root_dir: sci root_dir of every descriptor: shards run into <root_dir>/simulations/<shard>, and `merge` links them into <root_dir>/simulations/<name>.
_scarab_path: A private clone of scarab main, so sci's in-place hash checkouts can't disturb a working checkout.
_binary: Every setup's binary: scarab_<hash>, or HEAD for scarab_path's HEAD when gen runs. A policy can name its own.
_pick: Which gsearch point to use: best (the converged incumbent, the report's headline) or max_point (the best measured point).
_baseline: The baseline config for sci --visualize / --perf-analyze on the merged experiment.
_groups: Suites that share a traces_dir and run settings. Each group runs as one `cloudhost sweep` of its own descriptor (json/<name>_<group>.json); every group writes the one experiment <name>. traces_dir: where the group's traces are (on pakuchi, and at the same path on cloud machines). shard_size: cloudhost sweep --shard-size: a suite with at least this many simpoints is cut into shards of every setup x (this many // #setups) simpoints of like estimated runtime (cloudhost's split_shards). mem_per_sim_gb: cloudhost --mem-per-sim, one reservation for every sim of the group's sweep (null: cloudhost sizes each shard from sim_cost.json: its workloads' measured peak +15%, scaled for binaries with scarab PR #61, at least 3.8 GB). where: cloudhost --where. slow: the group's shards go first and prefer the fastest machines (--slow-suites). max_parallel: sims at once if a shard runs on pakuchi (a cloud shard runs as many as its slice). The shard sizes came from `fullsweep.py estimate` (README).
_suites: Per suite: enabled (or --suites / --skip-suites), its group, simpoint selection (top_simpoint N or simpoint_coverage fraction; every top_simpoint must be equal, since the merged descriptor holds all suites), warmup (null: the trace's whole warmup from the workload DB, which is 10M for datacenter and 50M for SPEC), params added to every setup for this suite only (through workload_params), simulation_type, and optional subsuites / workloads lists.
_policies: One sci configuration each, named by its key. `params`: Scarab flags. `mlp`: REPL_MLP on the gsearch study's base params, with gammas from core:all (the one static point for every suite), core:gi=0, core:gd=0, simpoint / input / workload / suite (each unit's own best, set through workload_params), or [gamma_i, gamma_d]. `fallback`: the levels a unit gsearch never searched takes its gammas from, in order, ending in a core unit (default: input, workload, core:all for simpoint; core:all otherwise).

lru._doc: Baseline: golden_small's MLC policy (REPL_TRUE_LRU). The gsearch gains are over this.

mlp_core._doc: REPL_MLP, one static (gamma_i, gamma_d) for the whole sweep: the core unit `all`.

mlp_gd._doc: REPL_MLP, best gamma_d with gamma_i = 0: the core unit `gi=0`.

mlp_gi._doc: REPL_MLP, best gamma_i with gamma_d = 0: the core unit `gd=0`.

mlp_sp._doc: REPL_MLP, each simpoint's own best pair where gsearch searched it (google top 6, others top 3); every other simpoint of the sweep falls back to its input's best, then its workload's, then core:all.

mlp_wl._doc: REPL_MLP, each workload's (benchmark's) best pair, given to all its inputs. Off by default (replaced by mlp_sp).

emissary_r1._doc: REPL_EMISSARY with R(1/1): every S&E miss is marked.

lacs._doc: REPL_LACS (20) at the MLC with its defaults.

clip._doc: REPL_CLIP (25) with its defaults (32 sampled sets, theta 25%).

drrip._doc: DRRIP, the baseline of a DRRIP-boost study such as dr1. Off by default.

_pakuchi_suites: Suites whose traces are all on pakuchi, for estimates with pakuchi in --pool (cloudhost checks the real files).
